data_notes: 91+ day auction tail RECONCILED 2026-07-19 to the NSS Delinquency Report (Travis-approved): tail/buckets now come from delinquent_leases (per-lease days_late/$) via delinquency_query.site_aging(), NOT facility_day Hummingbird unit buckets. tail_units = delinquent leases with days_late >= 90 (the report's auction_tail edge); the site and the report now show the SAME tail.
Tail trend tracks the delinquent_leases snapshot history, which begins 2026-07-18 (the series restarted from that source on reconciliation; it deepens daily with the ingest).

Net move-ins (league + current-month trend point) RECONCILED 2026-07-19 to Nectar's own MTD counter (facility_day.net_move_ins_mtd_msr) via portfolio_query.move_activity_mtd_msr() — the same source the weekly MTD PDF and travismorrow.com/portfolio KPI tiles use — replacing the daily-sum (which ran a few units low). Stays offline (read from the store the daily ingest populates).

Monthly trend series REBUILT 2026-08-10: every closed month is queried from the portfolio datastore BY MONTH (portfolio_query.closed_month_point) — the same source the Portfolio Snapshot PDF cites — replacing the snapshots/history_*.jsonl EOM cache, which is a one-time backfill with a hard end date that nothing extended when a month closed. Under the old path 2026-07 was never written: it ran all July as the open month, then fell out when August became current, and August would have gone the same way in September. A month now enters the series by existing in the store.

trends.window is a CALENDAR window — 14 complete months plus the current one, always 15 rows, never a record count. A month the store cannot answer is emitted as an explicit null row (has_data=false) and listed in trends.window.months_missing; it is never omitted, and the window never slides backwards to make up the count, so a gap stays visible as a gap. Only the current month carries partial=true. Each closed point records the as_of date it was read at and month_end_exact=false if the ingest missed the month's last day.

trends.brands rolls the same window up per brand server-side; portfolio.html also rolls brands up client-side from its own facility→brand map, so the two are reconcilable rather than separately trusted.
ROAS uses the latest closed ad-spend month; facilities with no paid campaigns show null, never a fabricated 0.
Auction-watch goal: 2 units portfolio-wide (Travis's operational target for the 91+ tail).
